production.scenario: Microsoft Teams notification fanout assigns tenant mailboxes to stateless workers so failover does not reshuffle the whole fleet.
components: global chat and meeting events waiting for push fanout to devices
service boundary that accepts tenant-scoped work and selects a worker owner
control-plane service that uses rendezvous hashing to rank workers per tenant and pick the stable owner
durable authority in Cosmos DB for worker membership, weights, and drain intent
send pushes, webhooks, and retries for the tenants they currently own
control path that removes workers gracefully before deployment or fault isolation
observability path for reshuffle size, worker imbalance, and tenant failover time
flows: The dispatcher receives a tenant-scoped batch of notification work from the global event bus.
The boundary invokes rendezvous hashing to rank the current worker set for that tenant.
The scoring service uses the authoritative membership and weight view from the worker registry.
The top-ranked worker receives ownership of the tenant batch with minimal reshuffle.
The drain controller writes upcoming maintenance intent before a worker leaves the fleet.
Only tenants whose top-ranked worker changed are remapped after the roster update.
Telemetry shows how many tenants moved, how even the load is, and how long failover took.
